faq.a: A U-bend, or trap, holds a small amount of water in its dip. That water seals the pipe so drain gases cannot rise into the room, while waste water can still flow through.
asks: What is a trap in plumbing?
Why is there water in the pipe under the sink?

faq.a: Waste breaking down in drains and sewers gives off gases such as hydrogen sulfide, which smells of rotten eggs. Traps stop that gas reaching your home.

faq.q: Why does a sink smell when it has not been used for weeks?
faq.a: The water in the trap slowly evaporates. Once it is gone, there is no seal, and drain smells come up. Running the tap refills the trap.

faq.q: Why do things get stuck in the U-bend?
faq.a: The bend is the lowest point where water sits still, so heavy things like rings, hair and grease settle there. Most traps unscrew so you can clean them out.
asks: How do you get a ring out of a sink drain?

faq.q: Does a toilet have a trap too?
faq.a: Yes. The curved pipe built into the back of a toilet bowl is a trap, and the water you see in the bowl is its seal.
asks: Why is there always water in the toilet bowl?

facts: A plumbing trap uses a small pool of trapped water as a seal against drain gases.
The water in an unused trap can evaporate over a few weeks, letting drain smells in.
